In this paper we will show that for a quasicompact quasiseparated scheme X the hypercomplete pro-étale \infty -topos, as introduced by Bhatt and Scholze, is equivalent to the \infty -category of continuous representations of the Galois category \mathrm{Gal}(X) of X with values in the \infty -category of pyknotic spaces. In particular this proves that internally to pyknotic spaces, the hypercomplete pro-étale \infty -topos of X is an \infty -category of presheaves.

1. Introduction Main results For a quasicompact quasiseparated scheme X X , the Galois category Gal ⁡ ( X ) \Gal(X) of X X , as introduced in [ 1 ] , is defined to be the ∞ \infty -category of points of the étale ∞ \infty -topos X e ´ ​ t X_{\et} of X X . This ∞ \infty -category turns out to be a 1 1 -category and admits a rather concrete description: The objects are given by geometric points of the scheme X X and the morphisms by specializations of such. In [ 1 ] , the authors refined Gal ⁡ ( X ) \Gal(X) to a pro- ∞ \infty -category whose underlying ∞ \infty -category recovers the ∞ \infty -category of points of X e ´ ​ t X_{\et} . We can therefore make use of the ideas of condensed or pyknotic mathematics introduced in [ 2 ] , [ 4 ] , [ 13 ] and consider Gal ⁡ ( X ) \Gal(X) as a pyknotic ∞ \infty -category. Recall that a pyknotic ∞ \infty -category is defined to be a hypersheaf of ∞ \infty -categories on the site of profinite sets and we can consider Gal ⁡ ( X ) \Gal(X) as such via the assertion K ↦ Fun ⁡ ( K , Gal ⁡ ( X ) ) K\mapsto\Fun(K,\Gal(X)) for a pro-finite set K K . Here we denote by Fun ⁡ ( K , Gal ⁡ ( X ) ) \Fun(K,\Gal(X)) the ∞ \infty -category of functors of pro- ∞ \infty -categories from K K to Gal ⁡ ( X ) \Gal(X) . Given two pyknotic ∞ \infty -categories 𝒞 \mathcal{C} and 𝒟 \mathcal{D} , we can from the ∞ \infty -category Fun cts ⁡ ( 𝒞 , 𝒟 ) \Fun^{\operatorname{cts}}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D}) of continuous funtors between them (see Definition 3.3 ). Let 𝒮 π \mathcal{S}_{\pi} denote the ∞ \infty -category of π \pi -finite spaces. We can regard 𝒮 π \mathcal{S}_{\pi} as a discrete pyknotic ∞ \infty -category 𝒮 π disc \mathcal{S}_{\pi}^{\disc} , by considering the constant sheaf on profinite sets with value 𝒮 π \mathcal{S}_{\pi} . In this language the exodromy equivalence (see [ 1 , Corollary 0.5.2, Corollary 13.6.3] ) says that there is a natural equivalence Fun cts ⁡ ( Gal ⁡ ( X ) , 𝒮 π disc ) ≃ X e ´ ​ t constr \Fun^{\operatorname{cts}}(\Gal(X),\mathcal{S}_{\pi}^{\disc})\simeq X_{\et}^{\operatorname{constr}} between the ∞ \infty -category of continuous functors from Gal ⁡ ( X ) \Gal(X) to 𝒮 π disc \mathcal{S}_{\pi}^{\disc} and the ∞ \infty -category of constructible étale sheaves on X X . As explained in [ 1 ] , the above equivalence holds in greater generality in the setting of so called spectral ∞ \infty -topoi (see [ 1 , Theorem 0.4.7, Definition 9.2.1] ). These are ∞ \infty -topoi 𝒳 \mathcal{X} , equipped with a geometric morphism f ∗ : 𝒳 → Sh ⁡ ( S ) f_{*}\colon\mathcal{X}\to\Sh(S) , where S S is a spectral topological space, such that f ∗ f_{*} exhibits the ∞ \infty -category Pt ⁡ ( X ) \operatorname{Pt}(X) as an S S -stratified space (see [ 1 , Proposition 9.2.5] for the precise statement). In this case 𝒳 \mathcal{X} is called a spectral S S -stratified ∞ \infty -topos. The main example to keep in mind is the canonical geometric morphism X e ´ ​ t → X Zar X_{\et}\to X_{\operatorname{Zar}} for a qcqs scheme X X , from X e ´ ​ t X_{\et} to the ∞ \infty -topos X Zar X_{\operatorname{Zar}} of Zariski-sheaves on X X . To any spectral S S -stratified ∞ \infty -topos 𝒳 \mathcal{X} , one can associate a pro- ∞ \infty -category Π ^ ( ∞ , 1 ) S ​ ( 𝒳 ) \hat{\Pi}_{(\infty,1)}^{S}({\mathcal{X}}) , called the profinite S S -stratified shape of 𝒳 \mathcal{X} , whose underlying ∞ \infty -category recovers the ∞ \infty -category of points of 𝒳 \mathcal{X} . In this setting Barwick-Glasman-Haine show that there is an equvialence Fun cts ⁡ ( Π ^ ( ∞ , 1 ) S ​ ( 𝒳 ) , 𝒮 π disc ) ≃ 𝒳 S ​ − constr \Fun^{\operatorname{cts}}\big(\hat{\Pi}_{(\infty,1)}^{S}({\mathcal{X}}),\mathcal{S}_{\pi}^{\disc}\big)\simeq\mathcal{X}^{S\operatorname{-constr}} between the ∞ \infty -category of continuous representations of the profinite S S -stratified shape Π ^ ( ∞ , 1 ) S ​ ( 𝒳 ) \hat{\Pi}_{(\infty,1)}^{S}({\mathcal{X}}) of 𝒳 \mathcal{X} and the ∞ \infty -category 𝒳 S ​ − constr \mathcal{X}^{S\operatorname{-constr}} of S S -constructible objects in 𝒳 \mathcal{X} [ 1 , Theorem 0.4.7 and Definition 9.4.7] . In the case 𝒳 = X e ´ ​ t \mathcal{X}=X_{\et} , this recovers the previous equivalence. The goal of this paper is to extend the results above to a larger class of sheaves. For this we recall from [ 2 , Construction 4.1.4] that we can equip the ∞ \infty -category of pyknotic spaces Pyk ⁡ ( 𝒮 ) \Pyk(\mathcal{S}) with the structure of a pyknotic ∞ \infty -category via the assertion K ↦ Pyk ⁡ ( 𝒮 ) / K . K\mapsto\Pyk(\mathcal{S})_{/K}. We denote the resulting pyknotic ∞ \infty -category by 𝐏𝐲𝐤 ⁡ ( 𝒮 ) \IPyk(\mathcal{S}) . The main theorem of this paper identifies the ∞ \infty -category of continuous representations of Π ^ ( ∞ , 1 ) S ​ ( 𝒳 ) \hat{\Pi}_{(\infty,1)}^{S}({\mathcal{X}}) with values in 𝐏𝐲𝐤 ⁡ ( 𝒮 ) \IPyk(\mathcal{S}) as follows: Theorem 1.1 . Let S S be a spectral topological space and 𝒳 \mathcal{X} an S S -stratified spectral ∞ \infty -topos. Then the exodromy equivalence induces an equivalence of ∞ \infty -topoi 𝒳 pyk → ≃ Fun cts ⁡ ( Π ^ ( ∞ , 1 ) S ​ ( 𝒳 ) , 𝐏𝐲𝐤 ⁡ ( 𝒮 ) ) \mathcal{X}^{\pyk}\xlongrightarrow{\simeq}\Fun^{\operatorname{cts}}\big(\hat{\Pi}_{(\infty,1)}^{S}({\mathcal{X}}),\mathbf{Pyk}(\mathcal{S})\big) between the pyknotification 𝒳 pyk \mathcal{X}^{\pyk} of 𝒳 \mathcal{X} and the ∞ \infty -category of continuous functors from the profinite stratified shape Π ^ ( ∞ , 1 ) S ​ ( 𝒳 ) \hat{\Pi}_{(\infty,1)}^{S}({\mathcal{X}}) to the ∞ \infty -category of pyknotic spaces. Here the pyknotification 1 1 1 The pyknotification was introduced in [ 2 , Construction 3.3.2] under the name solidification . is defined as the ∞ \infty -category of hypersheaves on the category of pro- S S -constructible sheaves Pro ⁡ ( 𝒳 S ​ − constr ) \Pro(\mathcal{X}^{S\operatorname{-constr}}) where the topology is generated by finite families that are jointly effective epimorphisms (see Definition 2.10 ). The 1 1 -categorical analogue of this construction was already considered in [ 13 , §7.1] . It follows from Example 7.1.7 of loc. cit. that for a qcqs scheme X X , the pyknotification X e ´ ​ t pyk X_{\et}^{\pyk} is equivalent to the ∞ \infty -topos of pro-étale hypersheaves X pro ​ e ´ ​ t hyp X_{\proet}^{\hyp} on X X as defined by Bhatt-Scholze in [ 3 ] . This means that the process of passing from a spectral ∞ \infty -topos to its pyknotification can be viewed as a generalization of the passage from the étale to the pro-étale ∞ \infty -topos for a scheme X X . Combining this alternative description of X pro ​ e ´ ​ t hyp X_{\proet}^{\hyp} with Theorem 1.1 we arrive at the following Corollary: Corollary 1.2 . Let X X be a qcqs scheme. Then the exodromy equivalence induces an equivalence of ∞ \infty -topoi X pro ​ e ´ ​ t hyp → ≃ Fun cts ⁡ ( Gal ⁡ ( X ) , 𝐏𝐲𝐤 ⁡ ( 𝒮 ) ) . X_{\proet}^{\hyp}\xlongrightarrow{\simeq}\Fun^{\operatorname{cts}}(\Gal(X),\IPyk(\mathcal{S})). In particular, the above theorem says that from a pyknotic point of view, the hypercomplete pro-étale ∞ \infty -topos is naturally equivalent to the ∞ \infty -category of internal copresheaves on the pyknotic ∞ \infty -category Gal ⁡ ( X ) \Gal(X) . This result has several interesting implications, some of which we try to explain in this article. First of all, many of the convenient properties of the pro-étale topos are now purely formal consequences of Theorem 1.1 . For example the fact that the pro-étale topos is locally weakly contractible [ 3 , Proposition 4.2.8] can easily be deduced using our main result (see section 5). Also it is a direct corollary of Theorem 1.1 that, contrary to the étale setting, for any morphism f : X → Y f\colon X\rightarrow Y of schemes the functor f ∗ : Y pro ​ e ´ ​ t hyp → X pro ​ e ´ ​ t hyp f^{*}\colon Y_{\proet}^{\hyp}\rightarrow X_{\proet}^{\hyp} has the surprising property that it commutes with all small limits (Corollary 4.18 ). This generalizes [ 3 , Corollary 6.1.5] where this was shown for closed immersions only. Our main theorem furthermore gives a conceptual explanation why the pro-étale topos has so many convenient categorical properties. It is, in the pyknotic sense, just an ∞ \infty -category of presheaves and thus inherits many nice properties of the much simpler ∞ \infty -topos Pyk ⁡ ( 𝒮 ) \Pyk(\mathcal{S}) of pyknotic spaces. Furthermore this opens the way to understanding the pro-étale topos using pyknotic higher category theory (i.e. higher category theory internal to the ∞ \infty -topos Pyk ⁡ ( 𝒮 ) \Pyk(\mathcal{S}) ). We will develop the basics of higher category theory internal to an ∞ \infty -topos in ongoing joint work with Louis Martini [ 14 , 15 , 16 , 17 ] . The language of pyknotic or condensed mathematics which we use in this article was developed by Barwick and Haine in [ 2 ] and independently at the same time by Clausen and Scholze in [ 4 ] . The only real difference between the two approaches is the way in which set-theoretic issues are dealt with. Since we will directly build on the results in [ 1 ] which are all formulated in the framework of [ 2 ] , we will do the same in this paper. The 1-categorical versions of many ideas and constructions in this paper already appear in [ 13 , §6 and 7] . Most notably the pyknotic category Gal ⁡ ( X ) \Gal(X) is already introduced there under the name Stone X e ´ ​ t constr \operatorname{Stone}_{X_{\et}^{\operatorname{constr}}} . This construction is then used to prove an analogue of the exodromy equivalence in this setting. See [ 13 , Theorem 2.2.2] and [ 2 , §4.3] . Technical Outline In the second section we will study categories of pro-objects and in particular effective epimorphisms in them. This will allow us to construct the effective epimorphism topology on Pro ⁡ ( 𝒳 0 ) \Pro(\mathcal{X}_{0}) for a bounded ∞ \infty -pretopos 𝒳 0 \mathcal{X}_{0} and thus define the pyknotification of a bounded coherent ∞ \infty -topos. It is quite elementary and may be mostly skipped by experts. The main technical result heavily used in the proof of Theorem 1.1 is an alternative description of the ∞ \infty -category of continuous functors Fun cts ⁡ ( 𝒞 , 𝐏𝐲𝐤 ⁡ ( 𝒮 ) ) \Fun^{\operatorname{cts}}(\mathcal{C},\mathbf{Pyk}(\mathcal{S})) for a pyknotic ∞ \infty -category 𝒞 \mathcal{C} . Namely we will see that it is equivalent to a suitably defined ∞ \infty -category of continuous left fibrations over 𝒞 \mathcal{C} (see Theorem 3.11 ). Providing this description and exploring a few consequences will be subject of the third section. In the fourth section we will proof Theorem 1.1 . The rough idea will be that the Exodromy equivalence together with the embedding 𝒮 π ↪ Pyk ⁡ ( 𝒮 ) \mathcal{S}_{\pi}\hookrightarrow\Pyk(\mathcal{S}) will provide an embedding 𝒳 S ​ − constr ≃ Fun cts ⁡ ( Π ^ ( ∞ , 1 ) S ​ ( 𝒳 ) , 𝒮 π ) ⸦⟶ Fun cts ⁡ ( Π ^ ( ∞ , 1 ) S ​ ( 𝒳 ) , 𝐏𝐲𝐤 ⁡ ( 𝒮 ) ) , \mathcal{X}^{S\operatorname{-constr}}\simeq\Fun^{\operatorname{cts}}\big(\hat{\Pi}_{(\infty,1)}^{S}({\mathcal{X}}),\mathcal{S}_{\pi}\big)\lhook\joinrel\longrightarrow\Fun^{\operatorname{cts}}\big(\hat{\Pi}_{(\infty,1)}^{S}({\mathcal{X}}),\IPyk(\mathcal{S})\big), which will extend to a fully faithful (see Proposition 3.32 ) embedding Pro ⁡ ( 𝒳 S ​ − constr ) ⸦⟶ Fun cts ⁡ ( Π ^ ( ∞ , 1 ) S ​ ( 𝒳 ) , 𝐏𝐲𝐤 ⁡ ( 𝒮 ) ) . \Pro(\mathcal{X}^{S\operatorname{-constr}})\lhook\joinrel\longrightarrow\Fun^{\operatorname{cts}}\big(\hat{\Pi}_{(\infty,1)}^{S}({\mathcal{X}}),\IPyk(\mathcal{S})\big). Since the pyknotification is by definition given by taking sheaves with respect to the effective epimorphism topology on Pro ⁡ ( 𝒳 S ​ − constr ) \Pro(\mathcal{X}^{S\operatorname{-constr}}) , we would now like to apply Theorem 4.1 , which would prove that Pro ⁡ ( 𝒳 S ​ − constr ) \Pro(\mathcal{X}^{S\operatorname{-constr}}) equipped with the effective epimorphism topology is also a generating site for the right hand side above. For this we have to show that the assumptions of Theorem 4.1 are satisfied which will occupy the vast majority of this section. Set theoretic conventions We will follow the set-theoretic conventions of [ 2 ] . In particular we fix a tiny and a small universe, respectively determined by two strongly inaccessible cardinals δ 0 < δ 1 . \delta_{0}<\delta_{1}. We recall that, for a strongly inaccessible cardinal δ \delta , a δ \delta - ∞ \infty -topos is a left exact accessible localization of Fun ⁡ ( 𝒞 , 𝒮 δ ) \Fun(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{S}_{\delta}) for a δ \delta -small ∞ \infty -category 𝒞 \mathcal{C} . We will simply say ∞ \infty -topos instead of δ 1 \delta_{1} - ∞ \infty -topos. By convention, a spectral S S -stratified ∞ \infty -topos 𝒳 \mathcal{X} will by always be a δ 0 \delta_{0} - ∞ \infty -topos. In particular, the ∞ \infty -category 𝒳 S ​ − constr \mathcal{X}^{S\operatorname{-constr}} of S S -constructible sheaves will always be tiny. Recall that the ∞ \infty -category of pyknotic spaces Pyk ⁡ ( 𝒮 ) \Pyk(\mathcal{S}) is defined to be the ∞ \infty -topos of hypersheaves with values in 𝒮 δ 1 \mathcal{S}_{\delta_{1}} on the site of tiny profinite sets equipped with finite jointly epimorphic families as coverings. Any profinite set can be covered by an extremally disconnected set K K and these have the property that any epimorphism T ↠ K T\twoheadrightarrow K of profinite sets has a section. Writing Proj \Proj for the category of tiny extremally disconnected sets we therefore have an equivalence Pyk ⁡ ( 𝒮 ) = Fun × ⁡ ( Proj op , 𝒮 δ 1 ) . \Pyk(\mathcal{S})=\Fun^{\times}\big(\Proj^{\operatorname{op}},\mathcal{S}_{\delta_{1}}\big). It follows that Pyk ⁡ ( 𝒮 ) \Pyk(\mathcal{S}) is hypercomplete and even postnikov-complete. See [ 2 , §2.2] for more background on pyknotic spaces. Theorem 1.1: Let S S be a spectral topological space and 𝒳 \mathcal{X} an S S -stratified spectral ∞ \infty -topos. Then the exodromy equivalence induces an equivalence of ∞ \infty -topoi 𝒳 pyk → ≃ Fun cts ⁡ ( Π ^ ( ∞ , 1 ) S ​ ( 𝒳 ) , 𝐏𝐲𝐤 ⁡ ( 𝒮 ) ) \mathcal{X}^{\pyk}\xlongrightarrow{\simeq}\Fun^{\operatorname{cts}}\big(\hat{\Pi}_{(\infty,1)}^{S}({\mathcal{X}}),\mathbf{Pyk}(\mathcal{S})\big) between the pyknotification 𝒳 pyk \mathcal{X}^{\pyk} of 𝒳 \mathcal{X} and the ∞ \infty -category of continuous functors from the profinite stratified shape Π ^ ( ∞ , 1 ) S ​ ( 𝒳 ) \hat{\Pi}_{(\infty,1)}^{S}({\mathcal{X}}) to the ∞ \infty -category of pyknotic spaces.

Corollary 1.2: Let X X be a qcqs scheme. Then the exodromy equivalence induces an equivalence of ∞ \infty -topoi X pro ​ e ´ ​ t hyp → ≃ Fun cts ⁡ ( Gal ⁡ ( X ) , 𝐏𝐲𝐤 ⁡ ( 𝒮 ) ) . X_{\proet}^{\hyp}\xlongrightarrow{\simeq}\Fun^{\operatorname{cts}}(\Gal(X),\IPyk(\mathcal{S})).

Recollection 2.1: Let 𝒞 \mathcal{C} be a tiny ∞ \infty -category. We define the ∞ \infty -category Pro ⁡ ( 𝒞 ) \Pro(\mathcal{C}) of pro-objects in 𝒞 \mathcal{C} to be the essentially unique ∞ \infty -category equipped with a functor i : 𝒞 → Pro ⁡ ( 𝒞 ) i\colon\mathcal{C}\to\Pro(\mathcal{C}) such that for any ∞ \infty -category with tiny cofiltered limits 𝒟 \mathcal{D} , precomposition with i i induces an equivalence Fun ′ ⁡ ( 𝒞 , 𝒟 ) → i ∗ Fun ⁡ ( 𝒞 , 𝒟 ) . \Fun^{\prime}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})\xrightarrow{i^{*}}\Fun(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D}). Here Fun ′ ⁡ ( 𝒞 , 𝒟 ) \Fun^{\prime}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D}) denotes the ∞ \infty -category of tiny cofiltered limit preserving functors. The ∞ \infty -category Pro ⁡ ( 𝒞 ) \Pro(\mathcal{C}) exists by the dual of [ 10 , Proposition 5.3.6.2] and is equivalent to Ind ⁡ ( 𝒞 op ) op \Ind(\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{op}})^{\operatorname{op}} . In particular Pro ⁡ ( 𝒞 ) \Pro(\mathcal{C}) is small and locally tiny but in general not tiny.

Recollection 2.2: Recall from [ 12 , Definition A.6.1.1] that an ∞ \infty -category 𝒳 0 \mathcal{X}_{0} is called an ∞ \infty -pretopos if i) The ∞ \infty -category 𝒳 0 \mathcal{X}_{0} has finite limits. ii) Finite coproducts exist in 𝒳 0 \mathcal{X}_{0} and are universal and disjoint. iii) Groupoid objects in 𝒳 0 \mathcal{X}_{0} are effective and their geometric realizations are universal. An ∞ \infty -pretopos 𝒳 0 \mathcal{X}_{0} is called bounded if 𝒳 0 \mathcal{X}_{0} is small and every object in 𝒳 0 \mathcal{X}_{0} is n n -truncated for some integer n n . If 𝒳 \mathcal{X} is a coherent ∞ \infty -topos in the sense of [ 12 , Definition A.2.0.12] , the full subcategory of 𝒳 < ∞ coh \mathcal{X}^{\operatorname{coh}}_{<\infty} spanned by the truncated and coherent objects is a bounded ∞ \infty -pretopos [ 12 , Example 7.4.4] . In fact any bounded ∞ \infty -pretopos arises this way by [ 12 , Theorem 7.5.3] . For more background on ∞ \infty -pretopoi and coherent ∞ \infty -topoi, the reader may consult [ 12 , Appendix A] or [ 1 , §3]

Example 2.3: If X X is a qcqs scheme, the ∞ \infty -topos X e ´ ​ t X_{\et} of étale sheaves on X X is coherent. In this case the ∞ \infty -category X e ´ ​ t , < ∞ coh X_{\et,<\infty}^{\operatorname{coh}} of truncated coherent objects is equivalent to the ∞ \infty -category X e ´ ​ t constr X_{\et}^{\operatorname{constr}} of constructible étale sheaves on X X , which is therefore an ∞ \infty -pretopos. In fact we more generally have an equivalence 𝒳 < ∞ coh ≃ 𝒳 S ​ − constr \mathcal{X}^{\operatorname{coh}}_{<\infty}\simeq\mathcal{X}^{S\operatorname{-constr}} for any spectral S S -stratified ∞ \infty -topos 𝒳 → Sh ⁡ ( S ) \mathcal{X}\to\Sh(S) [ 1 , Corollary 9.5.5] .

2.4: Let 𝒞 \mathcal{C} be an ∞ \infty -category with finite limits and geometric realizations of groupoid objects. Recall that a morphism f : X → Y f\colon X\rightarrow Y in 𝒞 \mathcal{C} is called an effective epimorphism , if the canonical morphism | C ˇ ​ ( f ) ∙ | ⟶ Y \lvert\check{C}(f)_{\bullet}\rvert\longrightarrow Y is an equivalence, where C ˇ ​ ( f ) ∙ \check{C}(f)_{\bullet} denotes the Čech-nerve of f f .

Lemma 2.5: Let 𝒳 0 {\mathcal{X}_{0}} be a tiny bounded ∞ \infty -pretopos. Let f ∙ : I → Fun ⁡ ( Δ 1 , Pro ⁡ ( 𝒳 0 ) ) f_{\bullet}\colon I\rightarrow\Fun(\Delta^{1},\Pro({\mathcal{X}_{0}})) be a tiny cofiltered diagram of effective epimorphisms. Then lim i f i \lim_{i}f_{i} , considered as a morphism in Pro ⁡ ( 𝒳 0 ) \Pro({\mathcal{X}_{0}}) , is an effective epimorphism.

Proposition 2.6: Let 𝒳 0 {\mathcal{X}_{0}} be an ∞ \infty -pretopos. Then 𝒳 0 {\mathcal{X}_{0}} admits a factorization system ( S L , S R ) (S_{L},S_{R}) (in the sense of [ 10 , §5.2.8] ), where S L S_{L} is the collection of effective epimorphisms and S R S_{R} the collection of ( − 1 ) (-1) -truncated morphisms.

Proposition 2.7: Let 𝒳 0 {\mathcal{X}_{0}} be a tiny bounded ∞ \infty -pretopos. Then the following hold: i) The collection of effective epimorphisms and ( − 1 ) (-1) -truncated morphisms form a factorization system on Pro ⁡ ( 𝒳 0 ) \Pro({\mathcal{X}_{0}}) . ii) A morphism in Pro ⁡ ( 𝒳 0 ) \Pro({\mathcal{X}_{0}}) is an effective epimorphism if and only if it can be written as a tiny inverse limit of effective epimorphisms in 𝒳 0 {\mathcal{X}_{0}} . iii) Effective epimorphisms are stable under pullback in Pro ⁡ ( 𝒳 0 ) \Pro({\mathcal{X}_{0}}) .

Lemma 2.8: Let 𝒳 0 {\mathcal{X}_{0}} be a tiny ∞ \infty -pretopos. Then finite coproducts are universal in Pro ⁡ ( 𝒳 0 ) \Pro({\mathcal{X}_{0}}) .

Corollary 2.9: Let 𝒳 0 {\mathcal{X}_{0}} be a bounded ∞ \infty -pretopos. Define a collection of morphisms { C i → D } i ∈ I \{C_{i}\rightarrow D\}_{i\in I} in Pro ⁡ ( 𝒳 0 ) \Pro(\mathcal{X}_{0}) to be covering if and only if there is a finite subset J ⊆ I J\subseteq I such that the induced map ∐ j ∈ J C j ⟶ D \coprod_{j\in J}C_{j}\longrightarrow D is an effective epimorphism in Pro ⁡ ( 𝒳 0 ) \Pro({\mathcal{X}_{0}}) . This defines a topology on Pro ⁡ ( 𝒳 0 ) \Pro({\mathcal{X}_{0}}) .

Definition 2.10: Let 𝒳 0 {\mathcal{X}_{0}} be a tiny bounded ∞ \infty -pretopos. We call the topology on Pro ⁡ ( 𝒳 0 ) \Pro({\mathcal{X}_{0}}) from Corollary 2.9 the effective epimorphism topology . For a bounded coherent δ 0 \delta_{0} - ∞ \infty -topos 𝒳 \mathcal{X} , we define the pyknotification of 𝒳 \mathcal{X} to be the ∞ \infty -topos 𝒳 pyk = Sh eff hyp ⁡ ( Pro ⁡ ( 𝒳 < ∞ coh ) ) . \mathcal{X}^{\pyk}=\Sh_{\eff}^{\hyp}\big(\Pro(\mathcal{X}_{<\infty}^{\operatorname{coh}})\big).

Remark 2.11: The pyknotification of a bounded coherent ∞ \infty -topos appeared first in [ 2 , Construction 3.3.2] under the name solidifcation . Since the word solidification is also used in [ 4 ] in an unrelated way, a different name is used here.

Example 2.12: In the case where 𝒳 = 𝒮 \mathcal{X}=\mathcal{S} , the ∞ \infty -category of bounded coherent objects in 𝒮 \mathcal{S} is the ∞ \infty -category of π \pi -finite spaces 𝒮 π \mathcal{S}_{\pi} . Let us write 𝒮 π ∧ \mathcal{S}_{\pi}^{{}^{\wedge}} for the ∞ \infty -category Pro ⁡ ( 𝒮 π ) \Pro(\mathcal{S}_{\pi}) of profinite spaces. It is shown in [ 1 , Proposition 13.4.9] that any pro-finite set admits and effective epimorphism from a profinite set. In other words the full subcategory Pro ⁡ ( Set fin ) ⊆ 𝒮 π ∧ \Pro(\operatorname{Set}^{\operatorname{fin}})\subseteq\mathcal{S}_{\pi}^{\wedge} is a basis for the effective epimorphism topology. It follows that we have an equivalence of ∞ \infty -topoi 𝒮 pyk ≃ Pyk ⁡ ( 𝒮 ) . \mathcal{S}^{\pyk}\simeq\Pyk(\mathcal{S}).

Example 2.13: More generally for a qcqs scheme X X , any object in Pro ⁡ ( X e ´ ​ t constr ) \Pro(X_{\et}^{\operatorname{constr}}) admits an effective epimorphism from an object in Pro ⁡ ( X ≤ 0 constr ) \Pro(X^{\operatorname{constr}}_{\leq 0}) by [ 2 , Proposition 3.3.8] . It follows that X e ´ ​ t pyk X_{\et}^{\pyk} is the hypercomplete ∞ \infty -topos associated to the 1 1 -topos Sh eff ⁡ ( Pro ⁡ ( X ≤ 0 constr ) , Set ) \Sh_{\eff}(\Pro(X^{\operatorname{constr}}_{\leq 0}),\operatorname{Set}) introduced in [ 13 , §7.1] . Thus [ 13 , Example 7.1.7] shows that X e ´ ​ t pyk X_{\et}^{\pyk} is equivalent to the hypercomplete ∞ \infty -topos X pro ​ e ´ ​ t hyp X_{\proet}^{\hyp} of pro-étale sheaves on X X defined by Bhatt-Scholze in [ 3 ] .

Remark 2.14: In principle we can also consider a version of the pyknotification where we consider the ∞ \infty -topos Sh eff ⁡ ( Pro ⁡ ( 𝒳 0 ) ) \Sh_{\eff}(\Pro(\mathcal{X}_{0})) of all sheaves with respect to the epimorphism topology instead of just hypersheaves. However there are reasons to prefer the hypercomplete version in Definition 2.10 . For example in many cases of interest the ∞ \infty -topos 𝒳 pyk \mathcal{X}^{\pyk} will be postnikov complete and even have a set of compact projective generators (see Theorem 5.7 ), which makes it much easier to work with. This will not hold for the non-hypercomplete version in general [ 2 , Warning 2.2.2] .

Definition 3.1: Let 𝒞 \mathcal{C} be any ∞ \infty -category with finite products. A pyknotic object in 𝒞 \mathcal{C} is a functor Proj op → 𝒞 \Proj^{\operatorname{op}}\to\mathcal{C} that preserves finite products.
